NDT training in San Antonio: how it works for San Antonio employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for San Antonio employers and technicians in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I, II and III. Theory runs live online, and practical training runs onsite at your facility, whether at Port San Antonio, a south-side plant or an Eagle Ford yard, under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice once you have completed classroom training, documented experience, the exams and a vision test.

San Antonio's NDT market is split in two, and the split matters. The first half is energy: a refinery on the east side, the Eagle Ford Shale to the south with its gathering lines, compressor stations and processing plants, the pipelines that carry product to the coast, and the power plants that serve the city. That work runs on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, with API and pipeline-operator requirements layered on top. The second half is aviation: the depot-level maintenance, repair and overhaul work at Port San Antonio, on the former Kelly Air Force Base, plus the military aviation at Joint Base San Antonio. That work usually runs on NAS 410 or equivalent aerospace personnel qualification, operator and OEM approvals, and military technical orders. The two halves use many of the same methods but qualify people differently. Technicians who understand both, and employers who know which one they need, get the most out of training.

Most people searching for NDT training in San Antonio are new technicians at inspection contractors serving the Eagle Ford and the refinery, manufacturing employees at automotive and industrial plants on the south side, aviation maintenance workers moving into NDT roles, or veterans with military NDT experience from the region's bases who want civilian certification. Atlantis NDT serves them with formal method training, exam preparation and Level III services. The certification is always issued by the employer.

Our scope is also clear. Atlantis NDT trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. San Antonio employers sometimes also ask for NAS 410 aerospace qualification, API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certification, AWS CWI or pipeline operator qualification. Those are separate schemes and requirements, and we do not train or certify to them. SNT-TC-1A method training provides the knowledge they build on. Ask us which credential a job actually needs before you spend money on the wrong course.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in San Antonio

All methods below are available to San Antonio employers and technicians as live-virtual theory, onsite cohorts at your facility, or blended. Content follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge and the employer's written practice, with practical work on real specimens. Required classroom and experience hours depend on method, level and written practice. See the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

MethodLevelsWhat San Antonio employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on refinery and midstream piping, vessel and tank shell inspection, pipeline girth-weld examination, aircraft structural inspection, and weld inspection in heavy fabricationLevel I: employer-defined education plus method training. Level II: Level I experience per the written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, II (Level III through UT)Encoded girth-weld inspection on pipelines, corrosion mapping on refinery and processing-plant equipment, and composite and structural inspection in aviationUT Level II strongly recommended
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, II (Level III through UT)Thick-section vessel welds and crack sizing at processing plants and the refineryUT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIPipeline and plant-piping weld radiography across the Eagle Ford and South Texas, casting and weld radiography in manufacturing, and aviation component radiographyTexas radiographer trainee or certification requirements, plus RT method training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIISteel weld inspection, oilfield equipment and pressure-control components, landing gear and steel aircraft parts, and automotive and industrial castings and forgingsMethod training and a vision test
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIAluminium and titanium aircraft and engine components, stainless process piping, and non-magnetic manufactured partsMethod training and a vision test
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld and equipment visual on every job, pipeline right-of-way and facility inspection, and borescope inspection in engine MROMethod training and a vision test (near vision and colour contrast)
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIAircraft structure and fastener-hole inspection, engine-component and wheel inspection in MRO, and heat-exchanger tube inspection at the refinery and power plantsBasic electricity and magnetism, and method training

The split shows up in the method choices. Energy employers lean on UT, PAUT, RT and MT. Aviation employers lean on ET, PT, UT and visual and borescope inspection. A technician with UT plus ET, or UT plus PT, can cross between sectors, which in San Antonio is a real career advantage. As we noted in the profile above, people qualified in both regimes are rare.

For technicians preparing for Level III, Atlantis NDT runs ASNT Level III exam preparation covering the Basic exam and method exams, delivered online.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in San Antonio, step by step

  1. Your employer's written practice. The written practice defines how the employer trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel: hours, exams, grading, vision requirements, recertification and the responsible Level III. See written-practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. Method training live-virtual, onsite or blended, to the hours in the written practice. Recommended figures are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience on real work, logged and signed. Busy midstream and pipeline construction seasons can build experience quickly. Keep your own copy of the log.
  4. General examination. A written exam on method principles.
  5. Specific examination. A written exam on the employer's procedures, codes and equipment, such as API 1104 acceptance criteria for pipeline work or ASME B31.3 for plant piping.
  6. Practical examination. A hands-on exam on real specimens with real discontinuities, administered and graded by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast testing per the written practice, repeated annually.
  8. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies you for the method and level, and the records are kept on file.
  9. Recertification. On the interval set by the written practice. Certification generally ends when you leave an employer, and a new employer re-certifies you, often crediting documented prior training and experience.

For RT specifically, Texas adds a state layer that sits alongside SNT-TC-1A. It is explained in the section below. The SNT-TC-1A guide covers the employer-based model in detail.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for San Antonio crews

Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in San Antonio or anywhere else. San Antonio employers can use three formats.

Live-virtual classroom. Instructor-led theory online, with real-time questions and exercises. This suits field technicians who rotate between San Antonio and Eagle Ford locations, and MRO workers on shift patterns. See online NDT training.

Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led instructor comes to your facility, which could be a contractor's yard, a plant or a hangar, for practical training and practical exams, bringing reference specimens or using yours. For controlled-access aviation or defence sites, you arrange instructor access or provide a training room outside restricted areas.

Blended. Theory online, practical onsite. This is the most efficient format for crews of several technicians.

Timing around the local work cycle matters. Refinery and processing-plant turnarounds absorb technicians for weeks. Pipeline construction follows project schedules. South Texas summer heat affects field practical sessions, so we often schedule outdoor practical work for early mornings or cooler months. MRO hangars run to aircraft induction schedules. We plan around all of these. Ask about onsite training for your San Antonio crew, and we will send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Larger programmes run through our corporate NDT training service.

Where NDT technicians work in San Antonio

Port San Antonio and aviation MRO. The former Kelly Air Force Base is now Port San Antonio, one of the country's larger aerospace maintenance campuses. Boeing runs the Department of Defense's heavy-maintenance depot for the C-17 Globemaster III fleet there. StandardAero runs a large engine MRO operation there, a centre for T56 turboprop engines used on the C-130 and for Rolls-Royce RB211-535 engines used on the Boeing 757. Commercial narrow-body heavy maintenance and other aerospace tenants fill the rest of the campus, and it has been expanding with new aerospace space. Engine and airframe MRO relies on ET, PT, UT, MT and borescope inspection, qualified under NAS 410 or equivalent aerospace schemes, with OEM and operator approvals and, for military work, technical orders such as TO 33B-1-1. SNT-TC-1A method knowledge carries over, but the personnel qualification system is different.

Joint Base San Antonio. JBSA-Lackland (which includes Kelly Field), JBSA-Randolph and JBSA-Fort Sam Houston together make San Antonio one of the largest military communities in the United States. Military NDT is done by service members trained in military programmes. After service, many of them look for civilian NDT careers in the region, which is where formal SNT-TC-1A training and certification come in.

Refining and the energy industry. Valero Energy, one of the largest independent refiners in the US, is headquartered in San Antonio. A refinery on the city's east side processes crude into fuels and specialty products. Refinery inspection uses SNT-TC-1A personnel for NDT, with API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors of record, and codes including ASME B31.3, ASME Section VIII and API 650/653.

Eagle Ford Shale. South and southeast of the city, the Eagle Ford play covers several counties, with production facilities, gathering lines, compressor stations, gas processing plants and crude and condensate pipelines heading to Corpus Christi and the Houston area. Pipeline weld inspection follows API 1104. Operators require pipeline operator qualification for covered tasks under federal pipeline safety rules, which is separate from NDT certification. Facility piping and vessels follow ASME B31.3 and Section VIII. San Antonio is the natural base for many of the contractors and technicians serving the play.

Manufacturing. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Texas builds full-size pickups and SUVs on the south side of San Antonio, with an on-site supplier park. Automotive and industrial manufacturing in the region uses MT, PT, UT and VT on welds, castings and forgings, often under customer quality requirements rather than a construction code. Cement plants along the I-35 corridor toward New Braunfels need UT thickness and weld inspection on kilns, mills and structural steel.

Power and utilities. CPS Energy, the city-owned utility, runs gas and coal-fired generation around San Antonio and co-owns the South Texas Project nuclear plant near Bay City. Power plants need ET on condenser and feedwater-heater tubes, UT on high-energy piping and boiler tubes, and MT and PT on welds during outages. Nuclear plant in-service inspection generally uses ANSI/ASNT CP-189 personnel qualification, not SNT-TC-1A.

Research. San Antonio is also home to Southwest Research Institute, a large independent research organisation with a long history of nondestructive evaluation research and development, including guided-wave and sensor technology for pipes and structures. It gives the city a depth of NDE engineering expertise unusual for a market its size.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program licenses industrial radiography under 25 TAC §289.255. Texas also has its own individual requirements. A licensee may not let anyone act as a radiographer trainee until that person holds a DSHS-issued trainee status card or a certification ID card. To get the trainee card, the person must complete an agency-accepted radiation-safety course. Full radiographer certification then requires the state's further training, experience and examination steps. These state credentials are separate from, and in addition to, SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Your RT method certificate says you can interpret a radiograph, and your DSHS card says you are authorised to work with the source. Apply through the DSHS online licensing system, and check current requirements with DSHS before mobilising a crew. For salary context, see our NDT salary guide. We do not publish local salary figures here.

Level III services and written practices for San Antonio NDT companies

San Antonio has many small and mid-sized inspection contractors, fabricators and aviation service companies, and they face the same problem. Customers audit their NDT programmes, and a written practice copied from an old employer, an outside Level III nobody can reach, or incomplete certification records will fail that audit. Atlantis NDT helps with:

  • Written practices built for what the company actually does, whether that is Eagle Ford pipeline work, refinery turnarounds or manufacturing. See written-practice development.
  • Outside Level III services, covering procedure approval, exam administration and grading, and certification sign-off. This is fully allowed under SNT-TC-1A for companies that do not need a full-time Level III.
  • Procedures and technique sheets for pipeline girth-weld UT and PAUT, corrosion mapping, RT technique and other specialised applications.
  • Programme audits ahead of operator or customer audits.

For aviation companies whose customers require NAS 410, we can explain how SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 differ, so you know where your programme stands. See the SNT-TC-1A guidance page. Book a Level III consultation to get started.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical exams test your process: set-up, calibration, coverage, evaluation and reporting. Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. San Antonio technicians can use the aircraft hangar environment for MRO-style inspections and the oil and gas site and storage tank environments for Eagle Ford and refinery work.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A must be done on real specimens with real discontinuities using actual equipment, graded by a Level III or designated examiner. For the written exams, work through our UT Level 2 practice questions and similar mock exams.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop sets the course content, oversees onsite and live-virtual delivery, and provides Level III oversight for employers who use Atlantis NDT's Level III services. See the full NDT training catalogue.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in San Antonio

How do I get NDT certified in San Antonio?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal method training, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Aviation MRO employers may qualify you under NAS 410 instead. For radiography, Texas also requires a DSHS trainee card or radiographer certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes. Method theory runs as live-virtual classroom sessions you can join from anywhere in Texas. The practical portion and practical exam need hands-on work with real specimens, and Atlantis NDT delivers that onsite at your employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours in your employer's written practice, the on-the-job experience you need and your exam schedule. Classroom time is the quickest part, and logging experience takes longest. See the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

The company needs a DSHS radiation license or registration. Individuals need a DSHS-issued trainee status card before working as a radiographer trainee, and radiographer certification to work as a radiographer. This is in addition to SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Check current DSHS requirements before starting.

What does NDT training cost in San Antonio?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, onsite versus online delivery and any Level III services you need. Cohort and onsite quotes are sent within one business day. Request a San Antonio training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by San Antonio employers?

Yes. Across energy, pipelines, fabrication and manufacturing, SNT-TC-1A is the standard personnel framework. Aviation MRO usually works to NAS 410 or similar aerospace schemes, which draw on the same method knowledge but have their own qualification rules. Because SNT-TC-1A is employer-based, a new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice.

Does your training qualify me for aviation MRO jobs at Port San Antonio?

It gives you the method foundation, but aviation employers usually qualify NDT personnel under NAS 410 or an equivalent aerospace scheme, with OEM and operator approvals for specific tasks. Our SNT-TC-1A training helps you prepare, and the aviation employer completes the aerospace qualification through its own programme.

Is ASNT certification enough for Eagle Ford pipeline work?

SNT-TC-1A covers your NDT method qualification. Pipeline operators also require operator qualification for covered tasks under federal pipeline safety rules, which is a separate requirement, and RT work needs Texas radiographer credentials. Contractors usually handle operator qualification as part of onboarding.

I have military NDT experience from a San Antonio base. How do I get civilian certification?

Military training and experience are valuable evidence, but they do not convert automatically. A civilian employer's Level III decides what credit to give under its written practice, and you will usually still need the general, specific and practical exams. Atlantis NDT can fill training gaps and prepare you for those exams.

Can you train our crew at our yard or plant in San Antonio?

Yes. Onsite cohorts run at your facility, with theory online first so onsite days are spent on practical work with your own equipment. In summer, we schedule outdoor practical sessions for cooler hours.

Our company needs a written practice and a Level III. Can you help?

Yes. Atlantis NDT develops written practices and provides outside Level III services, including exam administration and certification sign-off. Book a Level III consultation.

Do you offer Level III exam preparation in San Antonio?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation covers the Basic exam and method exams and is delivered live online for San Antonio candidates.
